text:
You hear Professor Beth Cartmill giving a presentation on traumatic brain injury to a group of medical professionals. 
You now have 90 seconds to read questions 19 to 24.
19. Professor Cartmill says that the greatest consequence of TBI is
the strain it places on a patient’s family.
20. Professor Cartmill suggests that TBI behaviour can be influenced by the
way it is viewed by members of the public.
21. Professor Cartmill feels that recognising someone’s emotional state is
more than simply mirroring their feelings.
central in establishing a bond between people.

22. Professor Cartmill mentions the case of her first participant in order to
illustrate the emotional torment resulting from TBI.
show a marked contrast between the features of TBI. 


23. What point does Professor Cartmill make about treatment options?
Further research into emotion recognition is needed.
All available interventions should be trialled.

24. Professor Cartmill recommends educating family members of TBI victims on how to
share their expectations concerning their loved one more openly.
